newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT--Dlr, bearish again, seen heading lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT--Dlr, bearish again, seen heading lower.

text.p: After a brief, failed attempt at conquering higher ground on Wednesday, the dollar is eyeing fresh losses on the near term, analysts predicted.
"I'm bearish on the dollar," said analyst Ben Morden at the consulting firm I.D.E.A.

"The pullback from 1.7070 marks took the wind out of that recovery," Morden said of the dollar's foray above 1.70 on Wednesday, coupled with a stint above 116.00 yen. "It's a clear topping pattern. The dollar will be plodding lower."
On Wednesday, the dollar closed at 1.6950/60 marks versus 1.7005/10 at the open, and at 115.83/88 vs. 115.65/77.

While dollar/mark attempted to revisit its intraday high of Tuesday at 1.7074, it lacked momentum to push to the next resistance level at 1.7120 -- the 62-percent retracement of the fall from 1.7389 on April 28 to 1.6680 on May 12.
"There should be good support at 1.6850 marks, then at 1.6775," said Morden who did not rule out a retest of the May 12 low down the road.
Morden was bearish as well on dollar/yen, "after we closed below 116.00 which indicates a short-term top."
The I.D.E.A. analyst put the next support on dollar/yen at 115.50, then at 115.09, the low on Tuesday.
Further down, dollar/yen would find very strong support at 114.50, an area of congestion, chartists predicted.
But the main factor of uncertainty for the dollar outlook is the European currencies' performance around the second round of the general elections in France on Sunday, they said.
A defeat of the center-right majority coalition may put France's participation in the European Monetary Union in jeopardy, some market watchers said.
"The D-mark has done well, climbing above 3.3785 French francs (resistance) and closing above that level. It may press toward the year's high of 3.3839 on February 4," Morden said.
"Breaking the 3.3839-franc level would trigger more D-mark strength across the board and that would play against the dollar too," Morden added.
Chartists expected dollar/Swiss -- which closed right at a key support at 1.4100/10 vs. 1.4180/90 at the open -- to be a bearer of bad news if the 1.4025/35 level gives way.
Morden expected that level to crumble soon, signaling a longer-term dollar slide to 1.62 marks, 1.38 Swiss francs and possibly 110.50 yen.
"But six months out, I'm bullish again on the dollar," Morden added. ((-- Isabelle Clary, 212-859-1666))
